items.title: Climate response to the Samalas volcanic eruption in 1257 revealed by proxy records
items.who: S. Guillet, C. Corona, M. Stoffel, M. Khodri et al.
items.note: Combined tree rings with medieval European chronicles to reconstruct the aftermath of 1257, showing how documentary series can test an attribution.

items.title: Volcanic stratospheric sulfur injections and aerosol optical depth from 500 BCE to 1900 CE
items.who: M. Toohey and M. Sigl
items.note: The eVolv2k database of sulfur injection estimates per event, assigning unidentified bipolar events a default equatorial source.

items.title: First identification of cryptotephra from the Kamchatka Peninsula in a Greenland ice core: Implications of a widespread marker deposit that links Greenland to the Pacific northwest
items.who: E. Cook, M. Portnyagin, V. Ponomareva et al.
items.note: First Kamchatkan glass found in Greenland ice, showing that North Pacific volcanoes must be considered as sources of Greenland signals.

items.title: VEILA: Identifying the source of unknown volcanic eruptions in Late Antiquity
items.who: University of Cambridge
items.note: Fellowship (2019–2021, €183,455) to locate the sources of unattributed sixth- and seventh-century eruptions through tephra in polar ice and equatorial lake cores.

items.title: THERA: Timing of Holocene volcanic eruptions and their radiative aerosol forcing
items.who: M. Sigl, University of Bern
items.note: ERC grant (2019–2024, €1.98 million) to fix the timing, sulfate magnitude and source location of all major Holocene eruptions from bipolar ice-core arrays.

items.title: Stratospheric eruptions from tropical and extra-tropical volcanoes constrained using high-resolution sulfur isotopes in ice cores
items.who: A. Burke, K. A. Moore, M. Sigl et al.
items.note: Uses mass-independent sulfur isotopes to tell stratospheric from tropospheric sulfate, so that bipolar spikes need not be assumed tropical.

items.title: Volcanic glass properties from 1459 C.E. volcanic event in South Pole ice core dismiss Kuwae caldera as a potential source
items.who: L. H. Hartman, A. V. Kurbatov, D. A. Winski et al.
items.note: Glass from the 1458 sulfate layer at South Pole is chemically unlike Kuwae products; Mount Reclus is named as one possible contributor.

items.title: Taking Earth's volcanic pulse: understanding global volcanic hazards by unlocking the ice core archive
items.who: W. Hutchison, University of St Andrews
items.note: Fellowship of £468,072 (2019–2023), renewed for 2023–2027 (£594,675), for ice-core tephra and sulfur-isotope work; Hutchison led the 2024 Zavaritskii attribution of 1831.

items.title: DFG Research Unit VolImpact: Revisiting the volcanic impact on atmosphere and climate
items.who: C. von Savigny, C. Timmreck et al.
items.note: Describes a German multi-institution research unit on volcanic forcing of atmosphere and climate whose members include authors of the 1809 'cold case' review.

items.title: Climatic and societal impacts of a "forgotten" cluster of volcanic eruptions in 1108–1110 CE
items.who: S. Guillet, C. Corona, F. Ludlow, C. Oppenheimer et al.
items.note: Used European and Japanese written sources with ice cores and tree rings to identify an overlooked cluster, a template for documentary attribution.

items.title: Smoking guns and volcanic ash: the importance of sparse tephras in Greenland ice cores
items.who: G. Plunkett, M. Sigl, J. R. Pilcher, J. R. McConnell et al.
items.note: Argues that sparse glass shards in Greenland ice can still fingerprint the volcanoes behind sulfate signals and should be sought systematically.

items.title: Cryptotephra from the Icelandic Veiðivötn 1477 CE eruption in a Greenland ice core: confirming the dating of volcanic events in the 1450s CE and assessing the eruption's climatic impact
items.who: P. M. Abbott, G. Plunkett, C. Corona et al.
items.note: A tephra tie-point confirms the ice-core chronology around the 1450s, fixing the date of the 1458 spike independently of its source.

items.title: The unidentified eruption of 1809: a climatic cold case
items.who: C. Timmreck, M. Toohey, D. Zanchettin et al.
items.note: Reviewed ice-core, instrumental and documentary evidence and modelled the climate response, concluding that source, season and exact year remain unknown.

items.title: The blue suns of 1831: was the eruption of Ferdinandea, near Sicily, one of the largest volcanic climate forcing events of the nineteenth century?
items.who: C. S. Garrison, C. R. J. Kilburn, D. E. Smart et al.
items.note: Discussion paper using reports of a blue and green sun in August 1831 to trace the aerosol plume to Ferdinandea, a claim later superseded by the Zavaritskii match.

items.title: Climatic, weather, and socio-economic conditions corresponding to the mid-17th-century eruption cluster
items.who: M. Stoffel, C. Corona, F. Ludlow et al.
items.note: Combines tree rings and written sources for the 1640s cluster, where candidate volcanoes such as Parker and Komaga-take lack tephra confirmation.

items.title: Volcanic stratospheric sulfur injections and aerosol optical depth during the Holocene (past 11 500 years) from a bipolar ice-core array
items.who: M. Sigl, M. Toohey, J. R. McConnell et al.
items.note: HolVol v1.0 extends the event list to 9500 BCE with magnitudes and approximate source latitudes for each sulfate signal.

items.title: The significance of volcanic ash in Greenland ice cores during the Common Era
items.who: G. Plunkett, M. Sigl, J. R. McConnell et al.
items.note: Systematic survey of tephra in Greenland sulfate layers of the Common Era, including the 1809 interval, often finding several sources per layer.

items.title: Lunar eclipses illuminate timing and climate impact of medieval volcanism
items.who: S. Guillet, C. Corona, C. Oppenheimer et al.
items.note: Uses dark total lunar eclipses in medieval chronicles to date stratospheric aerosol veils of 1100–1300, tightening timing for several unattributed events.

items.title: High sensitivity of summer temperatures to stratospheric sulfur loading from volcanoes in the Northern Hemisphere
items.who: A. Burke, H. M. Innes, L. Crick, K. J. Anchukaitis et al.
items.note: Sulfur isotopes across the 540s, 1450s and 1600s link the strongest cooling to extratropical eruptions, complicating a single tropical Kuwae source for 1458.

items.title: Evidence at source for the mid-fifteenth century eruption of Kuwae, Vanuatu
items.who: C. Ballard, S. Bedford, S. J. Cronin and S. Stern
items.note: Reviews historical, archaeological and volcanological evidence at Kuwae and argues for a major regional eruption while noting its global signature is unresolved.

items.title: Volcanic stratospheric sulfur injections from 500 BCE to 1900 CE, eVolv2k_version4
items.who: M. Sigl and M. Toohey
items.note: Current event table with injection estimates and attributed sources; 1230, 1286, 1695 and 1809 remain without a source.

items.title: Five Large 13th Century C.E. Volcanic Eruptions Recorded in Antarctica Ice Cores
items.who: J. Cole-Dai, D. L. Brandis, D. G. Ferris et al.
items.note: Antarctic and Greenland records show five large thirteenth-century eruptions, Samalas among them, most with bipolar signals suggesting low-latitude sources.

items.title: The 1831 CE mystery eruption identified as Zavaritskii caldera, Simushir Island (Kurils)
items.who: W. Hutchison, P. Sugden, A. Burke et al.
items.note: Matched cryptotephra in Greenland ice to proximal deposits of a remote Kuril caldera, resolving a nineteenth-century unattributed spike.

items.title: La mémoire orale du peuple de Kuwae, île mythique du Vanuatu
items.who: A. François and S. Bessis
items.venue: Journal de la Société des Océanistes
items.note: Studies oral traditions of the Kuwae eruption among Vanuatu communities, the main non-geological evidence for the event at source.

items.title: VOLTESSO: Volcanic climate forcing over the onset of the Little Ice Age through tephra geochemistry and stratospheric sulfate isotope analyses in polar ice cores
items.who: University of St Andrews
items.note: Fellowship (2026–2028, €260,348) using tephra and sulfur isotopes in polar ice to identify the sources of thirteen poorly attributed eruptions of 1150–1350 CE.

items.title: Precise dating of the 686 ± 2 CE Newberry Pumice eruption and insights into 7th century volcanism from cryptotephra and sulfur isotopes in Greenland ice
items.who: H. M. Innes, W. Hutchison, M. Sigl, J. R. McConnell et al.
items.note: Ties a Greenland sulfate signal to Newberry volcano, Oregon, extending the cryptotephra-plus-isotope attribution method to the seventh century.

items.title: Revisiting the eruptive nature of the 1108–1110 CE volcanic episode: Insights from sulfur isotopes and cryptotephra in Greenland ice cores
items.who: S. Ro, F. Brouillet, W. Hutchison, P. Sugden et al.
items.note: Preprint applying sulfur isotopes and cryptotephra to one of the largest sulfate events of 2,500 years to separate its eruptions and their altitude.
